argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification for launch readiness, but not caveat-free certification. Aggregate readiness clears threshold and there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which supports the release-level certification decision. At the same time, the same record shows a current unresolved weakness in the aviation maintenance triage use case, concentrated in deferred-defect routing, and the draft mitigation runbook remains incomplete because the alert threshold and accountable owner are still TBD. The supportable position is therefore not to oppose certification outright, but to treat the packet as supporting certification only with explicit model-card disclosure of that limitation and without claiming the draft runbook has already removed the disclosure obligation.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalating this as if certification were unsupported would overstate the gap in the record. The admissible evidence supports a narrower outcome: certification can proceed if the unresolved aviation maintenance triage limitation is explicitly disclosed. That preserves launch progress while keeping the packet aligned to policy and avoiding a false claim of clean compliance.
claims_about_policy: Under the stated policy, certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The current runbook does not meet that standard. The same policy separately requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Public model-card guidance and AI risk management guidance are consistent with that reading: disclose limitations and evaluation results, and use monitoring as an ongoing control rather than as proof that the limitation no longer exists.
concessions: The current record does not support any claim of caveat-free certification.
The draft mitigation artifact is not sufficient to eliminate the present disclosure requirement.
The model-card draft is currently inconsistent with the admissible evidence because it says there are no known material limitations.
